chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Saeed al-Samman, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) hastened the women at night from Al-Muzdalifa to Mina, and ordered those of them upon whom was a sacrificial animal (hady) that she should pelt (the Jamarah), and she should not depart until she has slaughtered (the animal); and those of them who did not have a sacrificial animal upon her, that she should go to Makkah until she has performed visitation (Ziyarah).
ai.seo_question: What are the different Hajj rituals for women with and without a sacrificial animal according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the practical flexibility granted to women during the Hajj rites, specifically regarding the transition from Muzdalifa to Mina. It distinguishes between women who have designated sacrificial animals (hady), who must remain to perform the stoning and slaughter, and those without, who are permitted to proceed directly to Mecca for Tawaf, reflecting the Prophet's (saww) accommodation of their needs.
